## Reproduction in the author's real environment

The first campaign ran on a bare VS Code. Re-run on a clone of the real environment: the same 145 extensions (APFS clone of `~/.vscode/extensions`), the same `settings.json`/keybindings/snippets/MCP config, and the same **8-folder multi-root workspace** (~10 GB, git repos included). OKF Studio is the default Markdown editor there, the window is 1440 px at DPR 2 with the explorer and the Chat panel open. The extension bundles are again unminified with source maps; the build queue is instrumented to log its debounce.

| Interaction | Bare VS Code | Real environment |
|---|---|---|
| Open a block editor | 350–390 ms | **673 ms** (webview JS 246 ms; same forced recalcs, each larger) |
| First render after opening the document | 285 ms | **457 ms** |
| **Commit (Cmd+Enter) → new version shown** | 655–680 ms, 1,755 ms first | **1,930 ms** (debounce 1,000) → 1,134 ms (450) → 590 ms (141) |
| Typing | p50 33 ms | p50 33 ms, max 177 ms |

### The adaptive debounce is what is felt

```
request debounce=40     built renderMs=457   ← first render after opening, under the load of 145 extensions
request debounce=1000   built renderMs=225   ← next commit waits 1 s before the render even starts
request debounce=450    built renderMs=71
request debounce=141    built renderMs=56
```

`currentDebounceMs()` = 2 × the last render, capped at 1,000 ms. In a loaded environment the first render after opening a document is slow (cold JIT + extension contention), so **the first commit after each opening waits ~1 s**, and the next one still waits twice the previous render. The slower the machine, the longer the wait: the heuristic amplifies the load. A commit from the preview is a single, final change; it should render at once (candidate fix 1 of this issue).

### Other extensions sharing the extension host

Extension host CPU during the first commit (975 ms of JS in total):

| Who | ms |
|---|---|
| GC (heap shared by all extensions) | 401 (55–65 on later commits) |
| `davidanson.vscode-markdownlint` (micromark re-parse of the whole document on change) | 265, then ~70 |
| this extension | 140, then 65–157 |
| `gruntfuggly.todo-tree` | 40–63 |
| `shd101wyy.markdown-preview-enhanced` | 31 |

They mostly run during our debounce window, so today they are hidden behind it; once the commit renders at once, they will compete with our render and patch planning. That makes host-side savings (parse5 run once, candidate fix 4) more valuable, and argues for posting the patch before the non-urgent host work (`incomingChanges` diff, properties table).

The webview side is the same as in the first campaign, only slower with DPR 2 and a narrower, taller page: fixes 2 and 3 still apply.
